newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: New U.N. chief names "provisional" cabinet.
newsitem.headline: New U.N. chief names "provisional" cabinet.

text.p: Kofi Annan, the new U.N. secretary-general, on Thursday announced "provisional" appointments to his executive office with Iqbal Riza of Pakistan named as chief of staff.
Riza was a peacekeeping official from Pakistan and the former U.N. representative to Bosnia.

Spokesman Fred Eckhard told reporters that appointments would be made final for his cabinet by the end of January and that he hoped to complete naming senior staff for various U.N. departments, such as peacekeeping, by the end of February.
Eckard said the new secretary-general was also considering appointing a deputy, a post not occupied for several years.

Meanwhile, Annan, a 58-year old U.N. career officer from Ghana who began his five-year term in office on Thursday, had asked and received the resignations of 23 undersecretaries-general and assistant secretaries-general, Eckhard said. Some of them, however, are expected to be reappointed.
Excepted from the group of resignations were special envoys working in the field in peacekeeping or peacemaking.

In addition to Riza, Rolf Knuttson of Sweden, director of political affairs, and Patrizio Civili of Italy, director of economic and inter-agency affairs, were also appointed to Annan's executive office. They both worked for Annan's predecessor Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

Others named included two executive assistants, both of whom worked for Annan in the peacekeeping department he headed before becoming secretary-general: Elizabeth Lindenmayer of France and Shashi Tharoor, who is also a best-selling Indian novelist.
In addition, there are two new senior officers in Annan's cabinet: Lamin Sise of Gambia and Diego Zorilla of Spain.
Eckhard, an American, is serving as acting spokesman, replacing Sylvana Foa, also an American, who has taken a year's leave of absence.

Not named to any post yet is Gillian Martin Sorensen, who nevertheless appeared during photo sessions in Annan's office among his senior staff. Sorensen, the wife of former President Kennedy's aide, Ted Sorensen, served under Boutros-Ghali as the controversial chairman of the U.N. 50th anniversary. Annan's aides would not say what post she will receive.
